content.comment_body: A bit of an odd question, but I've received my [product_name] with a DVD for [product_name] [version_no] and [product_name] [version_no]. (For the second software, the license key comes on a USB stick.) The problem is, my laptop doesn't have a DVD drive, and all I can find on the [company_name] website are demo versions. Is there any way to download the full versions online?
Perhaps you have a friend with a computer that has a DVD drive. You could copy the DVD contents to a USB stick.
After your suggestion, I did just that. I wanted to check here first in case there was any copy protection on the DVD. For future reference, you can simply copy all files onto a USB drive.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter difficulties installing [company_name] software distributed solely on DVDs, as many current laptops lack DVD drives. The main solution discussed is to use a different computer with a DVD drive to copy the files onto a USB stick; however, users are uncertain about potential copy protection and only find demo versions available for download on the official site.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect an easier, official way to access full licensed versions of purchased software, such as direct downloads or digital delivery options, rather than having to depend on physical media.
